stories.headline: Lula da Silva wins fourth term as Brazil president after defeating Flávio Bolsonaro
stories.body:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term as president of Brazil on Sunday. He defeated Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the election. Flávio Bolsonaro is the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. This presidential win is unprecedented in Brazilian history.

Lula da Silva previously served as president of Brazil between 2003 and 2011. He was imprisoned from 2018 to 2019 on corruption charges. Those charges were later overturned. He is 80 years old. During the vote count in São Paulo, leftist federal lawmaker Erika Hilton spoke about Lula da Silva. She called him a statesman and a giant.

Flávio Bolsonaro is 45 years old. He finished first in the first round of the presidential election. Former President Jair Bolsonaro led Lula da Silva by more than 2.2 million votes in that first round. Brazil has nearly 160 million registered voters. More than 33 million of those voters did not participate in the first round.

Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin issued an order on election day. Voting was extended nationwide across Brazil by two hours after his order. In Salvador, a court in Bahia ordered the arrest of a top transportation official. The arrest order was based on allegations of reducing public buses on election day.

When Reuters provided live coverage with over 78% of votes counted in the runoff, Lula da Silva led with 51.21%. Flávio Bolsonaro held 48.79% at that point. With nearly 99% of votes counted, Lula da Silva received 51.75% of the vote. Flávio Bolsonaro received 48.25% of the vote.

Pro-Bolsonaro congressman Nikolas Ferreira spoke to journalists during the election. He said either they win or they win. He added that people had been warned.

Former President Jair Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup. His political group remains powerful in parliament. Bolsonaro's Liberal Party and allied parties could control over 280 seats in Brazil's lower house. They could also control up to 50 seats in the Senate.

stories.headline: Israel prepares for general election with half a million new eligible voters
stories.body:
Half a million first-time voters are eligible to vote in Israel's general election. Around 70,000 Israelis are flying in from abroad to cast ballots. Arab citizens make up around one-fifth of Israel's population.

Gadi Eisenkot leads the centrist Yashar party in Israel. He is a former military chief of staff. His son was killed during the Gaza War. A participant in a pro-Netanyahu TV debate used a racist slur against Eisenkot. The participant referred to him as a Moroccan monkey. Eisenkot and other opposition party leaders ruled out forming a coalition government with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

US President Donald Trump publicly endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu for Prime Minister of Israel. A survey shows that over 70% of Jewish Israelis support establishing a state commission of inquiry into the October 7, 2023 attacks.

Billionaire American investor Bill Ackman and his wife Neri Oxman own a 5 percent stake in the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. Ackman said Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich should not serve in Israel's next government. He said they cause reputational damage. Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power party is projected to win around 10 seats in the Israeli parliament. Smotrich's Religious Zionism is projected to win 8 seats.

stories.headline: Aleksandar Vučić concedes defeat as Student List wins Serbia parliamentary election
stories.body:
Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat in his country's parliamentary election. He has dominated Serbian politics as prime minister or president since 2014. Last month, Vučić resigned from the presidency to trigger snap parliamentary elections.

Vučić said the Student List won between 135 and 140 seats. He said his own party won 105 seats. A poll sample by CeSID-IPSPS projected the Student List would secure 138 seats. The same poll projected the Serbian Progressive Party would take 104 seats. Cardiology doctor Ilija Srdanović led 250 candidates for the Student List. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen congratulated the Student List on its victory.

The collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad killed 16 people in November 2024. That event sparked nationwide student-led protests. Voter turnout reached 64.9% by 18:00 local time. Turnout reached 67.6% by 7pm local time, marking the highest level since 1992.

Vučić blamed independent media, unnamed European nations, and an American deep state for his defeat. Election monitors reported suspected voting irregularities. These included ballot photographing and attempted vote-buying. Serbian riot police cordoned off the election commission headquarters in central Belgrade on election day.

stories.headline: María Corina Machado returns to Venezuela after months in exile
stories.body:
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned home on Sunday. She had spent more than 10 months in exile. Machado is 59 years old. She fled Venezuela secretly on a speedboat in December 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway. Her movement, Vente Venezuela, launched an app to collect voter registration data from Venezuelans living abroad.

Machado returned by taking a private plane from Panama to Colombia and crossing overland. Supporters greeted her during a church service in Barquisimeto in Lara state. She called for new presidential elections to be held by July 2027.

US forces seized President Nicolás Maduro in January 2026. Maduro is jailed in New York on drug, weapon, and torture charges. The Trump administration backed Delcy Rodríguez as interim president after Maduro was captured. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said US-supported reconciliation talks allowed Machado's safe return.

US President Donald Trump said he knew nothing about her return. He added that the US is doing well in Venezuela. Trump had announced an oil deal with Venezuela in August 2026. He called it the biggest oil deal in world history.

stories.headline: Marine Le Pen launches campaign in Orléans amid widespread French protests
stories.body:
Marine Le Pen launched her French presidential campaign on Sunday. She spoke before 8,500 supporters in Orléans. Around 3,000 police officers were deployed in Orléans ahead of her rally to prevent anti-far-right unrest. Around 13,000 people attended a peaceful counter-rally against her National Rally party in Orléans on Saturday.

Her campaign launch occurred as cost-of-living and school condition protests swept France. Trade unions estimated 800,000 people participated in Saturday's protests. France's Ministry of the Interior reported that 410,000 people demonstrated nationwide on Saturday. That number included 110,000 demonstrators in Paris.

Authorities deployed over 70,000 police officers and gendarmes nationwide for Saturday's demonstrations. More than 1,300 arrests were made on Saturday. More than 2,000 people were arrested across France on October 17. The Interior Ministry reported 53 police officers were injured in clashes on Saturday. In Toulouse, a 20-year-old protester had several fingers severed when an explosive went off near him.

The French Senate will debate a proposed law to make vandals pay for property damage. Le Pen said vandals will spend their whole life paying. Leftist lawmaker Éric Coquerel warned the law would end street demonstrations. Cultural institutions including the Louvre closed or cancelled events on Saturday.

stories.headline: US midterm election ad spending passes ten billion dollars as Trump and Obama rally voters
stories.body:
Donald Trump attacked Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed during the US midterm campaign. El-Sayed is competing against Republican Mike Rogers for a US Senate seat in Michigan. Trump called El-Sayed a Jihadist Member of the Muslim Brotherhood on Truth Social. He alleged El-Sayed wants to impose Sharia law. Trump also claimed at a Port Huron rally that El-Sayed's mother worked for an organization that funded Osama bin Laden and Al-Qaeda.

At a Michigan rally, Trump encouraged crowd members to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj's appearance. Trump also claimed the US-Canada trade war would end soon because Canada is willing to give anything.

Former President Barack Obama campaigned in Detroit alongside El-Sayed and Jocelyn Benson. Obama joked that Trump has the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory. At an Ohio rally, Obama said Americans face higher living costs due to an unnecessary war.

Political ad spending for the 2026 US midterm election cycle has surpassed $10 billion. Spending is projected to reach $11.6 billion. Elon Musk donated $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund. He also donated $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC.

stories.headline: Bay of Bengal deep depression threatens Andhra Pradesh and Odisha with heavy rains
stories.body:
A weather system over the Bay of Bengal intensified into a deep depression on Saturday. The system was centered about 870 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam at 11:30 a.m. on October 25, 2026. Forecasters expect the system to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. It is forecast to cross as a very severe cyclonic storm by the forenoon of October 28, 2026. The cyclone is expected to bring maximum sustained wind speeds of 115 to 125 kmph. Wind gusts could reach 140 kmph.

Heavy rain forecasts cover several regions in India. Extremely heavy rainfall is forecast over Coastal Andhra Pradesh on October 27 and 28. Heavy rain is also forecast for Odisha and Telangana on October 28. Chhattisgarh is forecast to receive extremely heavy rainfall on October 28 and 29.

In Mankulam in Idukki, heavy weather caused a tree to fall on two cardamom plantation workers. Both workers were killed in the incident.

State governments have taken emergency measures. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu ordered a high alert. He prepared 10 National Disaster Response Force teams and 11 State Disaster Response Force teams for relief operations. Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited cancelled employee leaves. The power company established district control rooms to handle cyclone damage. District administrations in Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, and Alluri Sitharama Raju set up 24-hour control rooms. They also prepped relief centres.

The Odisha government cancelled leaves for district collectors, district magistrates, and critical officers. Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said that the government's primary objective is ensuring zero casualties. Majhi ordered all schools, colleges, and Anganwadi centres closed in five districts on October 28 and 29. Those districts are Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, and Malkangiri. Odisha deployed or placed on high alert 60 ODRAF teams, 17 NDRF teams, and 225 Fire Services teams ahead of the storm.

Cyclone warning signals were hoisted at nine ports. These ports include Chennai, Nagapattinam, Cuddalore, Karaikal, Pamban, and Thoothukudi.

stories.headline: BJP announces nationwide protests following Mallikarjun Kharge's comment about PM Modi
stories.body:
The Bharatiya Janata Party announced nationwide protests for October 26, 2026. The protests target Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge. Kharge made remarks directed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi's late father.

The incident occurred during an event in Patna marking the 139th birth anniversary of Bihar's first chief minister Shri Krishna Sinha. An audience member shouted at Kharge during the event. The audience member shouted that Modi will not go. Kharge responded to the heckler by saying that Modi's father will also go.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke out against the remarks. Shah said Kharge tore apart all norms of decorum with his comment in Patna. Shah claimed that repeated electoral losses over the past 12 years have driven the Congress party to desperation. He added that desperation has led Congress to the politics of slander. The BJP released a statement accusing Congress of using language associated with thugs. The statement accused Congress of functioning like a mafia gang.

BJP leader Nitin Nabin criticized opposition speech. Nabin said dragging departed family members into public speeches has become standard political culture under Rahul Gandhi. Kharge called ongoing opposition protests against electoral roll revisions the second war for independence.

Responding to a heckler in Patna, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said 'Modi ka baap bhi jayega'.

stories.headline: PM Modi opens RBI cybersecurity centre in Odisha and warns of banking cyber threats
stories.body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated a new data centre for the Reserve Bank of India in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. He also inaugurated a Cybersecurity Training Institute at the site. The facility was constructed at a cost of 169 crore rupees. It spans 18.55 acres at Info Valley-II in Jatni. The data centre features Tier IV accreditation across four independent facilities. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the facility will host mission-critical systems. Those systems include RTGS and NEFT payment rails.

During the event, Modi warned about cybersecurity threats. He said modern wars are fought by attacking national economies. He stressed the need to shield India's banking system from cyber terrorists. Modi also accused past Congress governments of practicing phone banking. He said past governments gave bank loans based on phone recommendations.

RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra spoke at the inauguration. Malhotra said information technology is now a core function of the central bank.

Modi provided figures on banking programs. He said that nearly 600 million Jan Dhan bank accounts have been opened. He added that 130 million individuals have become first-time entrepreneurs under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana. Approximately 2,100 police personnel were deployed to secure Bhubaneswar during Modi's visit.
